name: Chitosan filler

card.summary: An experimental chitosan-based injectable gel studied as an alternative to hyaluronic acid filler for restoring or adding facial volume.
card.note: Research-stage material; the sources describe laboratory and animal evaluation, not an approved product.

quick.overview:
Chitosan filler refers to experimental dermal fillers made from chitosan, a polysaccharide derived from chitin in crustacean shells. Fillers add volume under the skin to smooth lines or reshape contours, and researchers have explored chitosan as an alternative to hyaluronic acid (HA).
A 2022 paper describes a liquid chitosan formulation that turns into a gel at body temperature within about five minutes, needs roughly 4.7 times less injection force than HA, and held its volume longer than a commercial HA filler in an in vivo evaluation.
quick.how: There is no consumer product described in the sources. The research formulation is injected as a liquid and gels in place at body temperature.
quick.risks: It has not been reported in published human trials, so its safety and results in people are unknown.

lead: Chitosan is a polysaccharide made by deacetylating chitin, the structural material in crustacean shells and fungal cell walls. It is described as biodegradable and biocompatible and is used in wound dressings and tissue-engineering scaffolds [3].

Researchers have proposed it as a dermal filler to restore or add soft-tissue volume. A 2022 study introduced an injectable chitosan filler that transitions from liquid to gel at 37 degrees Celsius, noting that the standard cross-linked HA fillers require high injection force, can be broken down by enzymes and may produce granulomas [1].

The paper reports an injection force about 4.7 times lower than HA, a gel state reached within five minutes in vivo, a compressive strength about 2.4 times that of cross-linked HA, and a constant volume held longer than a commercial HA filler [1]. The authors expect it to be clinically applicable as a new material for dermal tissue restoration.

chain: Inject a liquid chitosan gel precursor
It gels in place and holds volume
Restores or adds soft-tissue volume in the treated area
angle.text: The intended payoff is the same as other fillers: added volume that smooths or reshapes a facial area. At present this is a research-stage material rather than an available treatment.

paras: The reported formulation is an injectable liquid that becomes a gel at body temperature, with high viscoelasticity and recovery after gelation [1].

Authors of the 2022 study compare it with HA, which requires large injection force and is easily broken down by enzymes [1]. A separate 2018 paper uses chitosan or collagen 'fillers' inside cellulose acetate scaffolds for tissue engineering, which is a different use of the word [2].
No studies found. Laboratory and in vivo (animal) evaluation of the chitosan filler is reported [1].

timeline.event: Chitosan dermal filler with enhanced moldability and elasticity reported [1].
